newsitem.title: CANADA: Wascana to consider Talisman meeting.
newsitem.headline: Wascana to consider Talisman meeting.

text.p: Wascana Energy Inc, which earlier rejected Talisman Energy Inc's C$1.7 billion takeover offer, will consider a Talisman request to meet with its board, Wascana chief executive Frank Proto said on Tuesday.
"(Talisman chief executive Jim Buckee) sent us a letter yesterday asking for a meeting with our board or special committee and they're taking it under advisement," Proto told a conference call.
However, Proto said he was confident that his firm could come up with an alternative to Talsiman's offer before it expired on March 24.

He said Wascana, which currently has two reportedly busy data rooms in Calgary, is considering all alternatives to the bid, including rival offers and financial restructurings such as income trust arrangements.

Regina, Saskatchewan-based Wascana said on Tuesday that its board unanimously rejected the offer after financial advisers RBC Dominion Securities Inc and Goldman Sachs & Co ruled that it was inadequate and that Wascana shareholders would have an insufficient equity stake in the merged entity.
It said the deal would give Wascana a value that was below that ascribed to oil and gas assets in similar transactions.
Wascana said also that Talisman's offer was announced before the release of the target's 1996 financial results, which showed stronger-than-expected oil and gas reserve additions and production.
Proto said Wascana had received a request from Talisman to gain data room access, a query that would also be examined by the company's special committee.

"Right now, everyone who has had access to the data room...have access on the same terms and conditions and we're reviewing what those terms and conditions may mean to someone who already has an offer out," he said.
Talisman has offered C$18.50 cash or 0.41 of a Talisman share for each Wascana share. The bid is valued at C$1.7 billion with the assumption of Wascana's long-term debt.

On Sunday, Wascana released its updated assessment of reserves which showed a total of 303 million barrels of oil equivalent in the proven plus probable category, a 24 percent jump from the number reported in 1996 financial results.

Wascana officials told the conference call that Ryder Scott Co, which made the evaluation, pegged the present value of the proven and probable reserves, discounted at 10 percent before tax, at C$2.3 billion.
The amount did not include land value.
Wascana shares were trading up 0.10 to 19.05 on volume of 1.9 million late in Tuesday's session.
Talisman fell 0.35 to trade at 43.90, placing the share-swap value of its offer at C$17.99 per Wascana share, the lowest since it launched the bid on February 12.
